turns.t: Doctor, I'm worried. Mum's been on steroid tablets for a long time, and I've read they can thin the bones.
It's only a small dose. I've been on them for ages. ~
Good questions, both of you. Mrs Rafferty, how long have you been on the prednisolone?
About five years, since the polymyalgia.
That's right, Mum, it was the year we moved.
Five years, thank you. What dose are you on?
Five milligrams, once a day.
Thank you. Any aches or pain in your back, any fractures, or loss of height?
No fractures. A little backache, now and then, for about two months.
It's six months, Mum. You were holding your back at Christmas.
So two months from you and six months from your daughter. I'll record it as two to six months.
She's lost height, Mum. You used to be taller than me.
I haven't.
I'll record that you say no, and your daughter says yes. I'll measure you today. Any other symptoms, bruising easily, or thin skin?
Bruises, yes, on my arms.
Any stomach upset, or black stools?
No.
What other conditions do you have?
She had polymyalgia rheumatica, which is why the steroids, high blood pressure, and an underactive thyroid.
Is there any family history of osteoporosis?
Her mother broke her hip at eighty.
And does she exercise, or smoke?
I walk a mile a day. I've never smoked.
Let me weigh and measure you, Mrs Rafferty. ~
Go on.
Weight 58 kilos, and your height is 154 centimetres. In your notes it was 160, six years ago.
I told you. ~
Oh. Well. ~
That's a loss of six centimetres, and it's a clue that the bones in your spine may be thinning.
Can you do something? ~
Yes. Long-term steroids do thin bones, and the earlier we protect them, the better. I'm going to prescribe a bone-protecting tablet, alendronic acid, 70 mg, once a week, with calcium and vitamin D.
Do I have to take more tablets? ~
Yes, but only one a week for the bone one. Take it first thing, with a full glass of water, and stay upright for thirty minutes.
I'll remind her. ~
I'd also like to arrange a bone density scan, and a blood test for your vitamin D and calcium.
Fine. ~
And walking is excellent. Keep it up. If you get sudden severe back pain, or you fall, come in the same day.
Thank you, doctor. ~
